title: Somebody finally pressed R. The video shortcuts are proven live — and the control found a key that is not ours.
firstRun: docs/migration/proof/retirement-step3-20260731221652/ — R/W/S already correct there; the run FAILED on its own control, which is the finding below.
reproduce: node docs/migration/tools/prepare-gplay-datadir.mjs <cue-probe-dual.mkv> <empty-dir> && node docs/migration/tools/retirement-step3-harness.mjs --datadir=<that dir>   (needs the Vite dev server on 5173; a prepared datadir is SINGLE-USE for playback, so build a fresh one per run)

whatWasClosed.standingItem: Slice 19 (2026-07-31) moved ten video.* registrations out of useMedia — where they acted on a videoRef that had been null in every window since slice 16 deleted the element that set it — into VideoCoreStudyOverlay, and re-pointed their catalog defaults onto R/W/S/;/'. It also found that effectiveKeys returned defaultKeys RAW while chordMatches compared against the always-normalized output of chordFromEvent, so 10 of 101 defaults could never match a keypress. Every part of that was proven by unit guard and source sweep, and slice 19, 20 and 21 each recorded the same open item: NOBODY HAS PRESSED R IN A RUNNING WINDOW.
whatWasClosed.why phase E did not already cover it: Phase E clicks [data-study-action] buttons. The keyboard path — window keydown -> chordFromEvent -> effectiveKeys normalization -> chordMatches -> the handler stack -> the overlay — shares only the final handler. It is a different path with a different failure mode, and it is the one a user actually uses.

measurements.measuredBy: capture-phase `seeked` events, not polled currentTime — phase E's own instrument, reused rather than re-invented. The cue controls resume playback, so a polled reading returns the cue start plus whatever played since; an earlier session read 2.96 against a real start of 2.15 and concluded the control was broken.
measurements.whyFocusIsRecorded: isTypingTarget() suppresses unmodified chords by design, so a stray focused input would read as 'the shortcut does nothing'. The phase blurs activeElement and records what it was.

keysAreSentLowercase.what: CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent sends key: 'r', which is what a real unshifted press produces. The catalog default is written 'R'.
keysAreSentLowercase.why: This only matches if slice 19's effectiveKeys normalization is still in place. If it regressed, this phase fails and the BUTTON phase above still passes — which is precisely the asymmetry that let the original defect live silently for a slice.

theControlFoundSomething.whatHappened: The first run used `q` as the unbound control. R, W and S were all correct in that run; the phase FAILED because `q` seeked to 0.
theControlFoundSomething.why: `q` is absent from this app's shortcut catalog, so it looked free. `KeyQ` is in the ADOPTED PLAYER's own vc_defaultKeybindings (vendor/seanime-web/app/(main)/_features/video-core/video-core.atoms.ts), which the catalog knows nothing about.

twoMaps.vendor: A B D E F H I J K M N P Q Z, plus BracketLeft/BracketRight and the arrows
twoMaps.controlMustBeFreeInBoth: x is in neither — the same test slice 19 applied when it chose R/W/S/;/' from what vc_defaultKeybindings leaves free.

theControlFoundSomething.isThisADefect: No, and it is not written up as one. `q` is not a Study OS binding and nothing in this app claims it. The finding is about HARNESS DESIGN: 'absent from our catalog' is not the same as 'unbound' in a window that also mounts a third-party player with its own keymap. Slice 19 already found the one case where that mattered for real — [ and ] dispatched a dead subtitle nudge AND the adopted player's speed control — and fixed it.
theControlFoundSomething.value: This is what the control is for. Without it the phase would have asserted only that SOMETHING seeks while keys are pressed; an auto-pause tick or a cue advance would have satisfied all three assertions equally.

gates.note: The change is confined to docs/migration/tools/retirement-step3-harness.mjs. No src/ file changed in this slice, so the src gates are re-run for confirmation rather than because anything could have moved them.

fullRunResult.phases: A taskbar identity, B window dragging, C real playback, E exact cue seeking by CLICK, G exact cue seeking by KEY, D quit with no orphan, F resume across restart

stillNotProvenLive: Blanc's toolbox player has still never been watched playing a file. The 23:25 attempt in proof/blanc-player-live-20260731232500/ ran with the sidecar STOPPED, so six of its eight phases are INFO, not PASS. This is now the oldest untouched item on the list.

The other six video.* rows the overlay registers (subEarlier/subLater/large, toggleAutoPause, toggleLoop, toggleFurigana) still have not been pressed. Phase G presses the three that seek, because a seek is measurable by a `seeked` event; the others change preferences or subtitle delay and need a different instrument.
Music keyboard navigation still does not exist, and must not be built by reusing video.* ids — registerCommandHandler is a last-registrant-wins stack.
